title: Rewrite multidplyr on mizu + mori
description:
Supersedes #163.

Replaces the mirai daemons with one work-stealing worker pool from [mizu](https://github.com/shikokuchuo/mizu). Data lives in shared memory and moves between processes as views, not copies. `partition()` shares the data once and slices it in parallel on the workers, so the host session holds no second copy. Verb results come back as zero-copy views for ungrouped data with plain columns, and as one serialization with no deep copy otherwise.

The pool gives no per-worker guarantees, so the per-worker functions are gone:

* `cluster_call()`, `cluster_send()`, `cluster_assign_each()`, and `cluster_assign_partition()` are removed, as is cluster subsetting with `[`.
* The new `cluster_map()` evaluates a function over a vector of inputs on the workers, for example reading one file per shard.
* `party_df()` now takes a list of data frames as shards.
* `cluster_assign()`, `cluster_copy()`, `cluster_library()`, and `cluster_rm()` keep their old interface but maintain a registry that multidplyr applies inside every verb evaluation.

Benchmark: 4 workers, 5M-row tibble (114 MB), median of 5 runs. The "100 × trivial call" row uses `cluster_call(cl, 1)` on #163 and `cluster_map(cl, 1, function(x) 1)` on this branch. Speedups are against the callr + qs2 column. Times below 0.05 s were measured to millisecond precision.

| Step | callr + qs2 | mirai + mori (#163) | mizu (this branch) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `new_cluster(4)` + first call | 0.73 s | 0.27 s | **0.23 s** | 3.2× |
| 100 × trivial call | 3.42 s | 0.06 s | **0.02 s** | >100× |
| `cluster_assign()` 40 MB vector | 0.17 s | 0.00 s | **0.00 s** | 85× |
| `partition()` 114 MB grouped df | 0.59 s | 0.20 s | **0.14 s** | 4.2× |
| grouped `summarise()` + `collect()` | 0.10 s | 0.02 s | **0.02 s** | 5× |
| `mutate()` + `collect()` | 0.33 s | 0.31 s | **0.06 s** | 5.5× |

The `mutate()` + `collect()` row shows the main win. On #163 every worker result pays a deep copy before it returns. On this branch the untouched columns of a result cross as small references, and only fresh columns serialize.

mizu is not on CRAN yet, so this branch cannot go to CRAN until mizu is. It runs on 64-bit Linux (kernel >= 5.3), macOS, and Windows.

title: Use mirai for workers and mori for sharing data
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Replaces callr sessions with mirai daemons (one compute profile per worker, so workers stay addressable and keep state) and replaces the qs2 tempfile in `cluster_assign()` with `mori::share()`. Requires R >= 4.3 (for mori).

Benchmark: 4 workers, 5M-row tibble (~120 MB), median of 5 runs:

| Step | callr + qs2 | mirai + mori | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| `new_cluster(4)` + first call | 0.73 s | 0.29 s | 2.5× |
| 100 × `cluster_call(cl, 1)` | 3.42 s | 0.12 s | 28× |
| `cluster_assign()` 40 MB vector | 0.17 s | 0.02 s | 8× |
| `partition()` 120 MB grouped df | 0.59 s | 0.24 s | 2.4× |
| grouped `summarise()` + `collect()` | 0.10 s | 0.02 s | 5× |
| `mutate()` + `collect()` | 0.33 s | 0.29 s | ~1× |

Worker results are materialised with `rlang::duplicate()` before returning, since they may otherwise reference shared memory the main process has already freed (regression test included).

title: dplyr 1.1.1 compatibility
description:
In dplyr 1.1.1, `auto_copy()` now throws a different and much improved error message. multidplyr was expecting the old error message in a test and wasn't using snapshot testing. https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/pull/6800

``` r
pf <- partition(data.frame(x = 1:6), default_cluster())
#> Initialising default cluster of size 2
df <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 3:1)

# Before
left_join(pf, df)
#> Error in `auto_copy()` at multidplyr/R/dplyr-dual.R:20:2:
#> ! `x` and `y` must share the same src.
#> ℹ set `copy` = TRUE (may be slow).

# After
left_join(pf, df)
#> Error in `auto_copy()` at multidplyr/R/dplyr-dual.R:20:2:
#> ! `x` and `y` must share the same source.
#> ℹ `x` is a <multidplyr_party_df> object.
#> ℹ `y` is a <data.frame> object.
#> ℹ Set `copy = TRUE` if `y` can be copied to the same source as `x` (may be slow).
```

title: Fixes for issues #6, #27 (or #21) #28 and #30. Added methods for rename_, tbl_vars and groups.
description:
This takes a slightly different approach than the pull request from @fugufisch, which first creates a cluster, and then reduces that cluster where needed. Here, `partition_` will by default create a cluster that never has more nodes than the number of shards. If the user passes a cluster that is too large, the same error as before will be generated.

Test case:

```
d_f <- data.frame(g = rep(LETTERS[1:3], 5),
                  v = rnorm(15))
d_f <- partition(d_f, g)
```

This will now initialize a cluster with 3 cores. Previously it would throw the following error (if sufficient cores were available):

> Error: length(values) == length(cluster) is not TRUE
